nodes.statement: Step 1: Reduction to a quadratic problem. By Lemma~ and Definition~, the loss in the lazy regime is well approximated by its second-order expansion around theta(0): cal L(t,D) = frac12Deltatheta(t)^top sf H Deltatheta(t) + langle b, Deltatheta(t)rangle + cal L(0, D) + o(1), where Deltatheta(t) := theta(t)-theta(0), sf H is the parameter-space Hessian assembled from \H_(nu)(0)otimes I_d\_nuin[N], and b is the residual gradient. The o(1) correction is uniform on the lazy-training ball by Part~9--10 of Lemma~. Thus the optimization problem reduces (up to higher-order terms) to minimizing a quadratic with eigenvalue spread [omegalambda/2,\;omegalambda_max]. Step 2: Apply Nemirovski--Yudin. For any first-order method on a strongly convex quadratic with condition number kappa = lambda_max/lambda_min, there exist initial conditions for which the loss after T gradient queries satisfies (Theorem~2.1.13 of citealpnes03; see also citealpny83): cal L(T) - cal L^* ge Big(fracsqrtkappa-1sqrtkappa+1Big)^2T cdot (cal L(0)-cal L^*). Translating to the gradient-flow setting requires a continuous-time limit. The standard reduction takes step size eta = 1/lambda_max and substitutes T to t/eta = tlambda_max: logBig(fracsqrtkappa - 1sqrtkappa + 1Big)^2T = -2T logfracsqrtkappa+1sqrtkappa - 1 approx -frac4Tsqrtkappa for kappatoinfty. Substituting Tto tlambda_max gives an exponential decay of rate 4lambda_max/sqrtkappa = 4sqrtlambda_minlambda_max. As etato 0 (continuous limit), the bound is preserved (it is step-size monotone in this regime), giving: cal L(t) - cal L^* ge expBig(-4sqrtlambda_minlambda_maxcdot tBig)cdot (cal L(0)-cal L^*). Since lambda_minge omegalambda/2 (Lemma~) and lambda_maxle omegalambda_max^(K) where lambda_max^(K) := max_nu lambda_max(H_(nu)'(0)/omega): cal L(t) ge expbig(-C_optcdot omegasqrtlambda lambda_max^(K)cdot tbig)cdot cal L(0). The geometric mean sqrtlambdalambda_max^(K) is not a single constant: it differs from lambda by a factor of sqrtkappa=sqrtlambda_max^(K)/lambda, which is poly(L,d,1/delta)^1/2 rather than O(1). We therefore retain sqrtkappa explicitly in the exponent (this is the unavoidable Nemirovski--Yudin condition-number gap; see Appendix~). Including the varepsilon^2 factor that arises when reading the loss in L^F(cal X) rather than parameter space (Part~15 of Lemma~, with the 1/n factor) and the 1/n from the average-loss normalization: cal L(sf T, D) ge c_2cdot exp\!left(-fracC_optcdot sqrtkappa\,omegalambda Ncdot varepsilon^2 cdot sf Tnright)cdot cal L(0, D). Step 3: Translate to compute. Using sf C = O(sf MTN), sf M=Theta(sf N^3) (Definition~) and varepsilon = xi/sf N (the choice that defines the data-limited boundary in Theorem~), and absorbing omega Nlambda into the constant poly(L,d,B,lambda): fracsqrtkappa\,omegalambda Nvarepsilon^2 sf Tn = sqrtkappa\,omegalambda Ncdot fracxi^2sf N^2cdot fracsf Csf MNcdot N = fracsqrtkappa\,omegalambda Nxi^2 sf Csf N^4 cdot sf Mcdot N le ThetaBig(fracsqrtkappa\,xi^2 sf Csf N^7Big), which yields: inf_Fin cal F_sf M, T, N(D)sup_Dincal DDeltacal R(F) ge c_2'cdot exp\!left(-C_opt'\,sqrtkappa\,xi^2sf C/sf N^7right)cdot cal L(0,D). The conversion from training-loss lower bound to excess-risk lower bound uses the standard fact that Delta cal R(F)ge \|F-F^*\|_L^F(cal X)^2 - O(xi^2/sf N) (cf.~Equation~), and the second term is dominated by the exponential in the Compute-Starved Stage where Equation~ fails.

Substituting into Equation~ (whose optimization term is exp(-2alphavarepsilon^2sf T/N)cdotcal L(0,D), with the 1/N factor from Remark~) gives the bound directly: inf_F in cal F_sf M, T, N(D) sup_D in cal D Deltacal R(F) leq O\!left(exp(-alpha\,xi^2\,sf T/sf N^3)right) + OBig(fracxi^2sf NBig), so this proof reduces to Condition 1 of Theorem~ with sf C = sf MTN, sf M, sf N fixed. Under varepsilon = xi/sf N, sf M = Omega(sf N^3), and T = widetildeOmega(sf N^3log/xi^2) (so the optimization term exp(-alphaxi^2sf T/sf N^3) is exponentially small in log(sf Ncdot Ld/xi^2)), the bound reduces to its statistical floor O(xi^2/sf N), recovering Condition 2 of Theorem~.
